title: Adaptive kernel autotuner: architecture & seq-len aware kernel picking
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add an online and offline autotuning subsystem that selects the optimal kernel variant for a model request based on detected hardware (arch), model architecture class, sequence length distribution, and batch size. The goal is to reduce per-token cost and tail latency by automatically choosing fused/low-memory kernels when appropriate and falling back to robust defaults when unstable.
background: We ship multiple kernel variants for attention and matmul paths (fused attention, segmented attention, tiled matmul with different tile sizes, int8/FP16 paths). Right now kernel choice is static at model load-time and tuned by hand for a few canonical configs. With more model families, quantization profiles, and hardware generations, static picks cause suboptimal throughput or OOMs for uncommon seq-len/batch combos. This ticket designs and implements heuristics and an autotuner to pick kernels dynamically and cache decisions per model+variant+env.
goals: Reduce P95 token latency by >=10% for long-prefill workloads (seq_len >= 1024) on Ampere A100 and H100-class nodes.
Reduce average token cost by >=8% across representative workloads via better kernel picks and quantization-aware choices.
Limit autotuner overhead to <1% of traffic and ensure safe automatic rollback on regressions.
Expose kernel decision telemetry and per-model decision history in Console for SRE/Customers.
non_goals: Automated model architecture search or quantization tuning beyond kernel variant selection.
Replacing the per-model pinned kernel option; we still allow explicit overrides for enterprise customers.
proposed_solution: Two-part system: (1) an offline microbenchmarking harness that runs candidate kernel variants against a matrix of (architecture, seq_len bucket, batch_size, model-type) to build an initial decision table; (2) an online lightweight probe/autotuner that validates and refines picks under production traffic and records results to a per-tenant decision cache. The runtime picks kernels at request scheduling time using the decision cache; if no match exists, it falls back to a conservative default and triggers a background probe job.
heuristics_overview: Detect hardware microarch and memory topology (A100/H100/RTX/AMD) and use it as a primary axis for decision keys.
Bucket sequence lengths into {short: <=64, medium: 65-512, long: 513-2048, xl: >2048} with ability to tune buckets per-model family.
Use model-class hints (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, mixture of experts) provided in model metadata to prefer fused kernels when semantics align.
Consider batch size and KV cache reuse: small-batch low-latency should prefer kernels optimized for single-token decode while large-batch prefill should pick throughput-optimized tiled matmul.
Weigh memory footprint vs compute: prefer int8 kernels only when quantization-quality checks passed and when peak memory is near device limit.
Penalty term for kernel-switching cost: if switching kernel would flush/resize KV caches or require layout transforms, add switching overhead to decision score.
Safety rule: never pick kernels that have previous OOM or correctness regression telemetry for the same model+env.
Cooldown and exploration: after a stable pick, allow periodic low-traffic exploration (1-2% sampling) for 24-72 hours to detect improvements on updated drivers or new load patterns.
Persist decisions keyed by model_id:arch:seq_bucket:batch_bucket:quant_profile with TTL and manual overrides visible in Console.
Enable an opt-out label (customer opt-out or high-security customers) to pin kernels and disable online probing.
Expose a per-decision confidence metric derived from comparison of P50/P95 and mem headroom across candidate kernels.
Fallback policy: if probe shows regression >5% P95 or any correctness anomaly, revert to last known-good kernel and flag for manual review.
Telemetry-driven defaulting: new models start with offline-harness recommended kernel for model family and arch.
Integrate with rollout policies: canary the tuner across a subset of capacity (region or dedicated pool) before global enablement.
autotuner_architecture: Compact description: a controller service (autotune-controller) collects microbench results and live probe telemetry, writes decisions to the decision cache (Redis-like fast store), and exposes an advisory API the serving runtime queries synchronously at route-prep time. Probe jobs run in isolated sandbox workers with configurable resource limits; results are scraped into telemetry with detailed metrics.
experiment_plan: Phase 1 - Offline sweep: run microbench matrix across archived models (gpt-like, t5-like, long-context models) on A100/H100 nodes. Collect latency/throughput/mem for each kernel variant and build baseline decision table.
Phase 2 - Staging canary: enable online probing for non-prod traffic on a small fraction of lanes; validate probe stability and rollback triggers.
Phase 3 - Production limited rollout: enable on <10% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor P50/P95, OOMs, correctness signals, and cost metrics.
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp to 100% with automatic rollback if cumulative regression thresholds exceeded.
Measurement: collect per-token latency histograms, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory high-water, OOM counts, kernel-switch count, and customer-level impact.
Bench harness: extend existing perf-bench service to support custom seq_len traces and KV-cache warm/cold runs.
Success criteria: see goals above; additionally confirm autotuner accuracy by sampling decisions and validating predicted wins vs observed.
acceptance_criteria: Autotune-controller and decision cache implemented and reachable from runtime; serving runtime reads decision within 1ms added median scheduling overhead.
Offline microbench outputs stored and used as initial decision table for at least three model families.
Online probe job runs without causing OOMs; probe overhead on production fleet <1% of GPU time.
Canary rollout completed with documented telemetry and no customer-facing regressions; roll forward to 100% toggled by SRE/PM.
Console surfaces per-model kernel decisions, confidence, and history; user can pin or override decisions.
End-to-end test: for a selected long-prefill workload, P95 improved by >=10% on A100/H100 in controlled run.
Documentation: runbook for debugging decision regressions, and an internal guide for adding new kernel variants to the harness.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probes could trigger OOMs or slowdowns. Mitigation: run probes in isolated sandboxes and limit probe batch sizes and runtime budgets.
Risk: noisy measurements may cause flip-flopping. Mitigation: require statistically significant wins with hysteresis and cooldown windows before switching.
Risk: increased system complexity. Mitigation: keep decision logic small in the hot path; heavy heuristics and aggregation live in controller not in runtime.
Risk: customer compliance objections. Mitigation: opt-out/pinning per-tenant and audit logs for kernel choice changes.
Risk: hardware driver updates change kernel performance. Mitigation: continuous offline sweeps on driver upgrades and version-tag decision entries by driver kernel version.
Risk: telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample and aggregate at 1s buckets and store detailed traces only for failures.
Risk: correctness regressions for fused kernels. Mitigation: include numeric and output-diff tests in harness and block auto-enablement until tests pass.
Risk: increased rollout blast radius. Mitigation: stepwise ramping, automatic rollback thresholds, and canary isolation.
Risk: model metadata missing or inaccurate. Mitigation: fallback to architecture-agnostic rules and treat missing metadata as lowest-confidence decisions.
